Found by ajc-truth (run 0054 s0008) while writing a docstring that claimed the opposite, and

THE FACT. AJC's leaf B needs SmoothOfRelativeDimension (genus C) (Pic0Scheme C).hom, and the
natural evidence available is a TANGENT SPACE dimension: dim_{kappa(e)} T_e Pic0 = genus C
(now proved at the headline, finrank_tangentSpace_pic0_eq_genus). It is easy to conclude that
mathlib offers nothing, because SmoothOfRelativeDimension is DEFINED by local standard-smooth
presentations and mentions no tangent space anywhere. I wrote 'it carries no bridge in either
direction, so this step is missing mathematics' and that is false.

converts relative dimension into a rank computation in both directions.

for 'tangent' or 'finrank' returns nothing, and that is a true fact about the name. The bridge
does not mention tangent spaces because it is stated in the invariant mathlib actually uses for
smoothness -- the module of Kaehler differentials. So the real obligation is not 'construct a
bridge' but 'translate between two invariants': rank Omega versus dim of the tangent space,
dual to each other over a field, plus the affine-local-to-scheme-level passage.

same mathematics in a DIFFERENT INVARIANT before recording it as missing. Tangent space vs
Omega, dimension vs rank, cotangent vs derivations -- these are the same content under names

######## I-0447
kind memory status open from None to None updated None
A GAP CAN LIVE IN A HYPOTHESIS'S QUANTIFIER, NOT IN MISSING MACHINERY -- and a CORRECT obstruction argument can point at the wrong thing

AJC cluster P carried 'the closed chi-ledger reaches only the effective cone; the negative part
needs an input the lane does not have' across THREE sessions -- a module docstring, four sibling
docstrings, a roadmap summary, an inbox item. It was false. chi_eq_of_bump (run 0055 s0008)
proves the ledger at EVERY Weil divisor from the same one-point bump that gave the effective cone.

WHY IT SURVIVED. The gap shipped with a proof sketch that is entirely CORRECT:
  - write D = D+ - (-D)+ as a difference of effective divisors;
  - the effective case handles each piece;
  - but chi is NOT additive in the divisor, and D is NOT linearly equivalent to D+, so neither
    of the lane's two transport mechanisms moves chi across the decomposition.
Every clause true. It even names the two candidate tools and correctly rules both out. Each
session re-derived it, found it sound, moved on.

What nobody questioned was the SHAPE of the hypothesis already in hand. hbump reads
  forall (P : PrimeDivisor) (E : WeilDivisor), chi (pointDivisor P + E) = chi E + residueDeg P
quantified over EVERY base divisor E, not just effective ones. So the telescope never had to
start at 0. Read the same identity as D+ = (-D)+ + D: the effective divisor (-D)+ telescoped
ONTO the base D. One induction (chi_telescope_list_add), compare with the effective-cone value
of chi(D+), done. No transport of chi across anything, and no new machinery.

THE MOVE TO REMEMBER: when a gap says 'we lack machinery M to get from A to B', before hunting
for M, re-read the QUANTIFIERS of the hypotheses you already have. Ask: at which arguments have
I been instantiating this, and at which am I ENTITLED to? A hypothesis quantified more
generously than the place it has been used is indistinguishable, in prose, from one that is
not -- and prose is what gets copied between docstrings.

COROLLARY ON PROVENANCE: a gap whose docstring carries a convincing obstruction argument is MORE
dangerous than one that just says 'open'. The argument discourages re-derivation while saying
nothing about whether it addresses the real question. When you inherit a gap with a good
argument attached, check what the argument is ABOUT before trusting its conclusion.

Related: [[axiom-check-lies-five-ways]] -- same family of defect (a check that passes while the
thing you care about is untouched).

`sorryAx`.  The clean/leaking split is worth summarising rather than eyeballing:

    lake env lean scripts/axiom-frontier.lean > /tmp/ax.txt
    python3 - <<'PY'
    import re
    entries = [e for e in re.split(r"\n(?=')", open('/tmp/ax.txt').read().strip())
               if e.startswith("'")]
    bad = [e.split("'")[1] for e in entries if 'sorryAx' in e]
    print(f'{len(entries)} probed, {len(entries) - len(bad)} clean, {len(bad)} carry sorryAx')
    for n in bad: print('  ', n)
    PY

several lines, so a per-line scan misclassifies exactly the declarations whose axiom
list is longest.  Measured 2026-07-28 through the root path, with `lake build
